h: Magna Carta, Bomber Command and Hartsholme Walks
p: A smaller wildlife park is a great antidote to a busy city break. Keep the visit simple, let the kids decide which animals deserve a second look, and don't feel you need to fill every minute. Countryside paths can be muddy after rain, so boots or wellies are a smart shout, and a flask of tea goes down well on a breezy Lincolnshire afternoon. Some smaller parks change their opening patterns outside the summer holidays, so a quick look at the latest updates before setting off is wise.

If you're heading back into the city, there's loads more to see. Inside Lincoln Castle, one of the original copies of Magna Carta, sealed in 1215, is on display in a purpose-built vault, alongside the Charter of the Forest. You can also walk the medieval walls for fantastic views over the cathedral and the city. It's the kind of history that sticks with older children.

On the southern edge of the city, the International Bomber Command Centre is a moving memorial and visitor centre dedicated to the men and women of Bomber Command during the Second World War. Lincolnshire was known as Bomber County, and the tall spire memorial is a striking sight.

For a gentler afternoon, Hartsholme Country Park on the south-west side of Lincoln has a lake, woodland trails and a play area, ideal for a picnic and a run-around. Whisby Nature Park, just outside the city, is another lovely spot for spotting birds around old gravel-pit lakes.

The Collection, a museum near the cathedral quarter, is another good rainy-day option, with archaeology from Roman Lincoln, when the city was known as Lindum Colonia, plus displays that bring the area's deep past to life for curious kids.
